exposure: Maternal lithium treatment in late pregnancy
cohort: Psychopathologically stable women with singleton pregnancies treated with lithium in late pregnancy, who had at least one maternal and neonatal lithemia at delivery, and their neonates.
finding: Despite a brief predelivery lithium discontinuation causing slight maternal lithemia fluctuations, lithium transferred completely across the placenta, leading to frequent but transient acute neonatal complications, most notably hypotonia, which was associated with higher neonatal lithemia.
